title: Large-scale empirical study on pairs trading for all possible pairs of stocks listed on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper proposes an automated pairs trading strategy based on three thresholds: starting (θ), profit-taking (ε), and stop-loss (Ω) for the spread between two highly-correlated stocks. Pairs are selected based on a Pearson correlation coefficient greater than 0.6 and stock volatilities within a range of 0.05 to 0.20 over a 250-day lookback period. The strategy is tested on all possible pairs of 1,784 stocks listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, evaluating winning probability and profit rate.
extraction.universe: 1,784 stocks listed on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange
key_findings: The profit rate becomes positive (totally positive arbitrage) in most cases of the possible combinations of thresholds.
The winning probability is unfortunately less than that of the 'draw case' pw = 0.5 in most choices of the thresholds.
An active pair producing a relatively large arbitrage can compensate the loss of wrong active pairs by choosing the threshold appropriately, leading to a positive profit rate.
The selection procedure of active pairs using correlation coefficients and volatilities works effectively to manage the asset safely by reducing risk.
limitations: Once a pair passes their decision time, the authors discard the pair and never recycle it again for pairs trading.
The game is simplified by restricting traders to always make a trade by a unit volume.
Transaction costs are not included in the main results, though the authors note they could be introduced to pare down candidates.
The results are based on historical simulations and cannot be used directly for practical pairs trading without further extensive analysis.
